To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the combination of Doppler lidars with other remote sensing instruments, such as a wind profiler and a cloud radar, allows the derivation of new information about the vertical motion of the atmosphere and the motion of atmospheric targets, such as water droplets or ice crystals.

the combination of vertical-velocity measurements by Doppler lidar and cloud radar allows the simultaneous measurement of the terminal fall velocity (and the size of water droplets) and the terminal fall speed (and the size) of ice crystals, and that the combination of wind profiler, Doppler lidar vertical-velocity measurements and cloud radar allows a comprehensive classification mask for vertically moving atmospheric targets.

the combination of Doppler lidars, wind profilers and cloud radars allows the simultaneous sensing of clear air and atmospheric targets and the correction for vertical air motion in precipitation measurements.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following aspects: (1) The combination of vertical-velocity measurements from three independent instruments, i.e., Doppler lidar (DL), cloud radar (CR), and wind profiler (WP).
the combination of three different types of vertical-velocity measurements and the synergistic use of the combined data set.

the development of new methods to improve and to combine vertical-velocity observations of Doppler lidars, cloud radars and wind profilers, and with the development of synergistic products that are not achievable with a single instrument.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this combination of three different instruments provides a unique set of measurements of atmospheric targets and vertical motion.
the combination of the instruments is very useful, but it is not a replacement of a Doppler lidar.
the combination of the three instruments provides a comprehensive vertical-velocity dataset that is not available with any single instrument.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the combination of instruments allows the simultaneous measurement of the vertical motion of the atmosphere and the motion of atmospheric targets.
the combination of instruments can provide a more detailed and more accurate picture of atmospheric targets than any single instrument alone.
we are able to detect the motion of the clear air and to detect and classify vertically moving atmospheric targets.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the combination of the three instruments provides a unique and powerful tool for the study of the vertical air motion in the atmospheric boundary layer and for the detection of atmospheric targets.
the combined vertical-velocity observations of the instruments can provide a more comprehensive picture of the atmospheric vertical motion and the terminal fall velocities of atmospheric targets.
the combination of vertical-velocity measurements with Doppler lidars and radars is a promising approach to obtain new and valuable information on the atmospheric boundary layer.
